Wherever the heap of those offerings falls, the Guru should assign to the disciple the name of the presiding deity of that sector—such as Keśava and so forth—followed by the title "Bhāgavata" or "Bhaṭṭāraka. However, for a Kṣatriya, the name should end in "deva"; for a Vaiśya, it should end in "pāla"; and for a Śūdra, it should end in "dāsa."

Then the preceptor, having removed the blindfold from the disciple and shown him the mandala of the lotus-circle, the preceptor, together with him, meditates upon the Lord Nārāyaṇa. He should then, according to the prescribed ritual, teach the twelve-syllable mantra along with the *praṇava*, its *ṛṣi*, *chandas*, and deity, as well as its ancillaries; thereafter, the eight-syllable mantra, and finally the *mūrti-mantras*. This is the procedure for Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas as well.
For Śūdras, women, and those born of mixed castes (*anuloma*), he should teach only the Vaiṣṇava names beginning with Keśava, excluding the *namaḥ*, *praṇava*, *huṃ*, *phaṭ*, and *svāhā* syllables.

Thereafter, having worshipped Hari residing in the water-pot and in the mandala, and having meditated upon him, the Guru—having visualized the mandala of the discus and lotus in his own hand and having made it the "Hand of Viṣṇu"—places it upon the head of the disciple who stands with palms joined in reverence. Then, in the presence of the fire, the preceptor shall instruct the disciple in all the traditional rules and observances (*ācāra-niyama*). As the mantra says: "The [mantra] of another must not be disclosed; one should not show the rosary (*akṣasūtra*); nor should one personally reveal the mudrās or the *siddhi-mantras*."

One should not speak ill of one’s teacher, nor should one transgress his commands. One should not revile one’s elders with speech, nor should one do what is displeasing to him. One should not step over the bed or other belongings of the teacher, nor should one leap over them. Even in the absence of the teacher, one should behave toward his wife as one would toward the teacher himself. One should always show respect to these three: the teacher, the Acyuta (the Lord), and the scripture. One should not touch atheists, those who have broken the bounds of propriety, or those who revile the Vedas and Brahmins; nor should one dwell with them, even in times of great distress.

One should never extend one's feet in the presence of the guru, the gods, or the sacred fire. One should always understand that the entire world is permeated by Vāsudeva. Without having worshipped the Lord of Gods, one should not engage in activities for one’s own nourishment. At the time of the *saṃdhyā*, one should perform recitation (*japa*), hymns of praise (*stotra*), prostrations, and so forth. One should always delight in meditating upon the Blessed Lord and performing those duties that ought to be done. Upon seeing Vaiṣṇavas and ascetics (*yatis*), one should bow to them on the ground. [One should renounce] children, wife, house, field, cattle, and other such wealth belonging to oneself.

One should address the Blessed One by his name in its entirety; being equal toward all beings and free from desire and anger, one should gradually withdraw the senses from their objects. One should practice the study of the scriptures together with those who are liberated from worldly existence, and always perform the rites prescribed by Śruti and Smṛti, and nothing else. The rites beginning with conception (niṣeka) and so forth should be performed according to the rules stated in one's own Sūtra; as for the secret name and the lineage (gotra), the natural [name] is desired and no other.

"Whether sitting, lying down, walking, or even while eating, one should glorify and constantly remember the eternal Vāsudeva. Having thus instructed the disciple in these observances, the Guru then performs the entire peace-offering (*śāntihoma*) ending with the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Then, having dismissed the fire, he bids farewell to the Deity residing in the pitcher and that in the mandala. He causes the disciple to recite benedictions. Thereafter, the disciple offers to the Guru cows, land, gold, ornaments, vehicles, male and female slaves, and so forth, according to his means.

Having fed the Brahmins and bestowed sacrificial fees upon them, and having eaten the remnants of the oblation right there, he should spend the remainder of the day. When the sun has set, adorned with all ornaments and permitted by his preceptor, he should enter his own decorated home together with his kinsmen. Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Ritual of Initiation," in the *Kriyākairavacandrikā* composed by the venerable Varāhaguru. The Twenty-seventh Chapter:
The Ritual of Worship (*Samārādhana-vidhi*).
Now the procedure for propitiation is described:

the preceptor, having bathed by means of one of the seven types of baths known as Vāruṇa, Divya, Āgneya, Vāyavya, Pārthiva, Māntra, and Mānasa; adorned with a white sacred thread, an upper garment, anointment with sandalwood paste and the like, and vertical marks (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) made with white clay; having performed his daily obligatory duties; having washed his feet up to the knees and his hands up to the wrists; having sipped water (ācamana); and having circumambulated the temple twice— [The text continues with the subsequent ritual steps.]

Having approached the side of the door and performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the mantras beginning with "To Ācakra," and standing upon the consecrated seat, he should clap his hands three times. Then, having opened the three doors of the three upper chambers with the mantra "Oṃ Kṣaṃ, obeisance to Tārkṣya"; the three doors of the three middle chambers with the mantra "Oṃ Śāntāya, obeisance"; and the three doors of the three lower chambers with the mantra "Oṃ Yaṃ, obeisance to Vāyu."

Having had the other doors opened by attendants or Brāhmaṇas with the mantra “Oṃ muktāya namaḥ,” and having entered the inner sanctum (garbhagṛha) on the right foot to the south of the Brahma-thread while chanting the Sāman hymn “Adhipātā i,” he should bow his head to the Lord with the twelve-syllable mantra, light the lamps, and discard the garlands, flowers, and other offerings.

The worship of the Vedicā, the vessel, and the image, beginning with Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa and ending at the Mahābali-pīṭha, should be performed according to the prescribed rules for installation by the disciple or an attendant, using the respective mantras beginning with *praṇava* (Oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*.

Adorned with all ornaments, the preceptor enters within; when the deity faces east or west, he himself faces north; when the deity faces south or north, he faces east. Sitting upon a tortoise-seat (kūrma-āsana) two *tālas* wide and one *tāla* high at the side of the deity, he should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūta-śuddhi*). "May the spirits, Piśācas, Pretas, and Guhyakas depart! Without causing obstruction to any of them, I shall commence the rite for Viṣṇu. May those Piśācas and spirits who dwell upon this ground depart!"

May those beings who create obstacles depart by the command of Hari. Following that, [I take refuge in] the tortoise and others in the divine world, then the jewel-encrusted pavilion, and there Śeṣa; upon him the throne of Dharma and the rest, above that the lotus and the female attendants holding chowries; Viṣṇu, the Goddess, the collection of ornaments and weapons, the serpent, the sandals, Vainateya, Senānī, the gatekeepers, and the hosts beginning with Kumuda—those devotees of Viṣṇu, I take refuge in them.

Having recited this, when the sound of musical instruments has been set forth outside, one should cover the entrance of the inner sanctum (*garbhagṛha*) without gaps using a curtain. Then, having invoked and worshipped [the deities]—saying "Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā" for the bell; "Oṃ, obeisance to the Discus" for the bud-shaped ornament (*mukula*); "Oṃ, obeisance to the Great Serpents" for the threads; "Oṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī" for the tongue; and "Oṃ, obeisance to Prajāpati" for the resonance—one should ring the bell.

Regarding the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) and the mantra for the seat (*āsana*): Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Atala is the meter (*chanda*), and Śrīkūrma is the deity (*devatā*); its application (*viniyoga*) is upon the seat. For the Earth: Kūrma is the seer, Satya is the meter, and Brahmā is the deity; its application is upon the seat. *Namaḥ brahmaṇe*.

Having worshipped the seat with: *Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ, obeisance to the glorious Anantāsana; oṃ, obeisance to Kamalāsana; oṃ, obeisance to Vimalāsana; oṃ, obeisance to Yogāsana; oṃ, obeisance to Vīrāsana; oṃ, obeisance to Kūrmāsana*, one should pray: "O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu. Do you, O Goddess, support me and make this seat pure. Purify me with riches; I bow to you, O Sovereign of the Gods. Thus having prayed.

Having assumed a posture such as the lotus (padmāsana) or the auspicious cross (svastikāsana), and having meditated upon the lineage of gurus by reciting: "Salutation to our gurus," "Salutation to our supreme gurus," and "Salutation to our parameṣṭhi gurus," one should thereafter perform the rites of drying and so forth.

The Self is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the body; Primordial Nature (*prakṛti*) and the Person (*puruṣa*) are the meters (*chandas*); Truth (*satya*) is the deity (*devatā*); its application (*viniyoga*) is for the seat. For the mantra *oṃ ātman*, the Self is the seer; the Person and Primordial Nature are the meters; Truth is the deity. *oṃ* salutation to Brahman; *oṃ* salutation to Viṣṇu; *oṃ* salutation to Īśvara; *oṃ bhūṃ* salutation to the Earth; *oṃ* salutation to both palms and backs of the hands; *oṃ* salutation to the two thumbs; *oṃ* *svāhā* to the two index fingers; *oṃ* *vaṣaṭ* to the two middle fingers; *oṃ* *huṃ* to the two ring fingers; *oṃ*... [to the two little fingers].

*Phaṭ* with the two little fingers; *oṃ nakhamukhebhyaḥ vauṣaṭ*. For the mantra of the Discus (*cakra*): Śambhu is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), the glorious Sudarśana is the deity (*devatā*), the syllable *ra* is the seed (*bīja*), *hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and red is the color; its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of binding the directions.

*Ācakrāya hṛdayāya namaḥ*, *oṃ vicakrāya śirase svāhā*, *oṃ sucakrāya śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*, *sūryacakrāya kavacāya huṃ*, *jvālācakrāya netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*, *sudarśanacakrāya astrāya phaṭ*. [Salutations to Him] who bears the discus, conch, bow, axe, sword, arrows, trident, noose, goad, thunderbolt, shield, plow, pestle, mace, and spear; who has most fierce fangs, flaming hair, three eyes, and carries a blazing chowrie, and is adorned with necklaces and armlets.

One should meditate upon the wheel that destroys the life-breath of all enemy hosts, situated within a hexagon. Having performed the placement of the wheel-gesture (*cakramudrā*) with: "Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the self of the Time-Fire (*kālavaiśvānara*); obeisance to the fire-fence-gesture (*agniprākāramudrā*); Oṃ, to the one with arrows, to the one with the Śārṅga bow, to the one with iron shafts, huṃ phaṭ, to the Sudarśana, svāhā; obeisance to the space-wheel-gesture (*ākāśacakramudrā*)."

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "For the sake of destroying all sins produced by ignorance and karma which obstruct the yoga of devotion to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, and for the purpose of propitiating the Blessed Lord, I shall perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*)," [one proceeds]. The Seer (*ṛṣi*) of the Praṇava is Brahmā; the Goddess Gāyatrī is the Metre (*chandas*); the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) is the Deity (*devatā*). *Aṃ* is the Seed-syllable (*bīja*); *Uṃ* is the Power (*śakti*); *Maṃ* is the Pin (*kīlaka*). Its color is white. It is applied for the purpose of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). *Nārāyaṇāya hṛdayāya namaḥ* (Salutation to Nārāyaṇa, the Heart). *Vibhave śirase svāhā* (To Vibhu, the Head, Svāhā).

*Vaṣaṭ* to the peaceful *Śikhā*. *Huṃ* to the *Kavaca* which illuminates the meaning of the *Praṇava*. *Vauṣaṭ* to the two *Netras* accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi. *Phaṭ* to the *Astra* of bliss. I constantly worship the all-pervading, peaceful Nārāyaṇa, who illuminates the meaning of the *Praṇava*, together with Śrī, Bhūmi, and Ānanda, within the lotus of the heart. Then, perform three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* consisting of *recaka*, *pūraka*, *kuṃbhaka*, and *recaka*. *Oṃ*, salutation to Yoga-mudrā. For the seed-syllable *vāyu* (*yaṃ*), Kiṣkindha is the *ṛṣi*; Jagatī is the *chandas*.

The great element, the material wind, is the deity. This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the purpose of drying up all sins committed through the actions of mind, speech, and body. O Wind, you who blow hither, you who blow thither, you whose form is such—you indeed travel as the messenger of the gods, the universal healer. These two winds blow: from the ocean and from the farthest distance. May one blow strength upon me; may the other blow away whatever is harmful. At the navel-center, *oṃ*, salutation to Vāyu.

By means of the form of smoke-colored Vaiśvānara Agni, who is the essence of the great wind, I dry up all the sins residing within my body. For the seed-syllable *agni*, Kāśyapa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Vaiśvānara Agni is the deity (*devatā*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of burning away all sins of our mental, vocal, and physical actions. "Agni wards off the Rākṣasas... O you of pure vows."

In the heart: *Oṃ vaiśvānarāgnaye namaḥ*. With the triangular, red-colored Vaiśvānara fire, I burn away all the sins residing within my body. For the Earth seed-syllable (*laṃ*): Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), and Viṣṇu in the form of the Boar (*Varāha*) is the deity (*devatā*). This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the purpose of stabilizing the risen fire at the throat. *Styonā pṛthivī... śarma saprathāḥ*. *Oṃ laṃ*: By means of the Earth seed-syllable and through touch, I stabilize the risen fire at the throat.

Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi) of the seed-syllable of nectar (amṛtabīja), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), and Soma is the deity (devatā). Its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of bathing our body with nectar. From the house where the wind blows... [the syllable] *guṃ* was produced by Āyu. Oṃ Vaṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa! With the streams of nectar arising from the round, crystal-colored seed-syllable of Varuṇa, I bathe my body from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head. To the Saṃhāramudrā in that state, obeisance.

Having thus displayed the *tattvasaṃhāramudrā*: for the seed-syllable of Earth (*pṛthvī-bīja*), Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), and Nārāyaṇa in the form of the venerable Varāha is the deity (*devatā*). *Oṃ laṃ laṃ laṃ*. I fill my body, from the feet up to the knees, with the element Earth—square-shaped, yellow in color, endowed with the sense organs of smell and the genitals, and possessing the qualities of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—by means of external inhalation (*pūraka*). Within that [element], [I worship] *Oṃ hrāṃ bhaṃ laṃ hrīṃ sakalarāṃ*, to Viṣṇu, the sovereign lord of Earth.

To Sadyojāta Nārāyaṇa, whose nature is the *nivṛtti-kalā*, *huṃ phaṭ*. While meditating on this mantra of Earth (*pṛthvī-mantra*), I dissolve the entire earthly element into that mantra by means of the *kumbhaka* breath-retention. *Oṃ taṃ namaḥ parāya sitavarṇāya gandhatanmātrātmane namaḥ*. I dissolve the mantra of Earth into the subtle element of smell (*gandha-tanmātra*). I cast that subtle element of smell into the great receptacle called Water (*toya*) by means of the *recaka* exhalation.

Oṃ ślāṃ ślāṃ ślāṃ! O earthly portion, from the feet up to the knees, from the square earthly mandala, enter into dependence upon the watery portion and become dissolved. Sindhudvīpa is the seer (ṛṣi) of the seed-syllable of water; Gāyatrī is the meter (chanda); Varuṇa is the deity (devatā). Oṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ! I fill my body with the waters—from the outside by means of inhalation—extending from the knees to the waist, which are joined with the tongue and the organ of excretion, shaped like a half-moon, white in color, and endowed with the qualities of sound, touch, form, and taste.

In the midst of that, meditating on the mantra: *oṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ rīṃ sakalarīṃ ambhodhipataye brahmaṇe vāmadevāya dhanurdharāya pratiṣṭhākalātmane huṃ phaṭ*, I gradually withdraw everything consisting of the syllable *aṃ* by means of the *sarvakumbhaka* into that mantra. *Oṃ ghaṃ namaḥ parāya pāṇḍaravarṇāya rasatanmātrātmane namaḥ*. I withdraw the mantra of the waters into the subtle element of taste (*rasatanmātra*).

I unite that subtle element of taste (rasatanmātra) with the subtle element of smell (gandhatanmātra) in the fire by means of exhalation (recaka). Hvāṃ hvāṃ hvāṃ! O aqueous portion, from the knees up to the waist—from the aqueous eight-petaled lotus—be dissolved into the fiery portion with dependence. For the seed-syllable of fire (agnibīja), Kāśyapa is the seer (ṛṣi); Triṣṭubh is the meter (chanda); Agni is the deity (devatā).

Oṃ raṃ raṃ raṃ: I fill my body from the external [space] up to the navel, starting from the secret place, with fire—triangular, pale-red in color, endowed with the eyes, feet, and sense organs, and possessing the qualities of sound, touch, and form—by means of inhalation (pūraka). Meditating upon the mantra "oṃ hrūṃ hrīṃ ṇyaṃ hrīṃ sakalarūṃ agnyadhipataye rudrāya ghorāya pradyumnāya vidyākalātmane huṃ phaṭ," I gradually withdraw all that is fiery into that mantra by means of breath retention (kumbhaka).

Oṃ daṃ, salutation to the one who is supreme, whose color is light, and whose nature is the subtle element of form; salutation. I dissolve the mantra of light into the subtle element of form. That subtle element of form, together with the powers of smell and taste, I unite with the air by means of the *recaka* breath. Hrāṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ! O fiery portion, from the secret place up to the navel, from the triangular fire-maṇḍala, become dissolved within the airy portion with dependence [upon it]. For the seed-syllable of air (*vaṃ*), Kiṣkindha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Jagatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Vāyu is the deity (*devatā*).

Oṃ yaṃ yaṃ yaṃ: I fill my body, from the navel to the nose, with the smoke-colored, circular Vāyu element—endowed with the skin and the sense of touch, and possessing the qualities of sound and touch—by means of external inhalation (pūraka). Meditating upon the mantra "Oṃ hraiṃ ṇaṃ sakalaraiṃ vāyvadhipataye īśvarāya tatpuruṣāya saṃkarṣaṇāya śāntikalātmane huṃ phaṭ" within that [element], I gradually withdraw the entire Vāyavya [element] by means of retention (kumbhaka) into that same mantra.

Oṃ Dhaṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, to the one of red color, whose essence is the subtle element of touch; salutation! I withdraw the mantra of Vāyu into the subtle element of touch. That subtle element of touch, together with the subtle elements of smell, taste, and form, I unite with the ether through exhalation (recaka). *Syaṃ syāṃ syāṃ*. O portion of Vāyu, from the wind-mandala marked with six dots, extending from the navel to the tip of the nose, become dissolved within the ethereal portion with full dependence. Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi) of the seed-syllable of ether, and Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ).

The Paramahaṃsa is the deity. Oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ! I fill my body, from the nose to the crown of the head, with the external ether—resembling the petal of a blue lotus, endowed with the organ of speech and hearing, and characterized by the quality of sound—by means of inhalation (*pūraka*). In its center, meditating upon the mantra "Oṃ hrauṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ sakalarauṃ, to Sadāśiva, the Lord of Ether, Īśāna, Vāsudeva, whose self consists of the *kalās* beginning with Peace (Śānti), huṃ phaṭ," I gradually withdraw the entire ethereal element into that mantra by means of retention (*kumbhaka*).

Oṃ Naṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, to the one of white complexion, salutation to the essence of the subtle element of sound (*śabdatanmātra*). I dissolve the subtle element of space (*ākāśatanmātra*) into the subtle element of sound. I dissolve that subtle element of sound, together with the subtle elements of smell, taste, form, and touch, into my own heart by means of the exhalation (*recaka*). Kṣmāṃ kṣmāṃ kṣmāṃ. O portion of the etheric realm, from the nose up to the crown of the head—from the ethereal sphere consisting of the two circles—be dissolved into your own heart along with all dependencies.

Oṃ Paṃ, salutation to the Supreme One of white and black color; salutation to the self of the principle of mind (*manas-tattva*). I dissolve the internal organ (*svānta*) into the ego (*ahaṃkṛti*). Oṃ Phaṃ, salutation to the Supreme One of pale-red color; salutation to the self of the ego (*ahaṃkārātman*). I dissolve the ego into the intellect (*buddhi*). Oṃ Baṃ, salutation to the Supreme One with the luster of crystal; salutation to the self of the principle of intellect (*buddhi-tattvātman*). I dissolve the intellect into primordial nature (*prakṛti*). Oṃ Bhaṃ, salutation to the Supreme One of white color; salutation to the self of primordial nature (*prakṛtyātman*). I dissolve primordial nature into the individual soul (*jīva*).

Oṃ Maṃ! Salutation to the one beyond the supreme, who has the luster of crystal; salutation to the self of the principle of the individual soul (jīva-tattva). Having placed the extremely subtle soul—which possesses the radiance of the sun and is free from the power of latent impressions—located in the navel-center, upon the upper part of the inner body by means of the breath-retention (kumbhaka) through the Suṣumṇā channel as fine as a lotus fiber, and having pierced the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) and emerged from the body, I unite it with the Supreme Brahman residing above in the white thousand-petaled lotus within the solar orb.

Oṃ maṃ haṃsaḥ! O Jīva, from the navel-cakra, by way of the *suṣumnā* path, become absorbed in the Supreme Self with devotion. [Performing the visualization] from the feet to the top of the head: Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Yoni-mudrā. Having thus displayed the mudrā: Oṃ lāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Universal Self, the glorious Nārāyaṇa; salutation. Oṃ vāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Nivṛtti, Aniruddha; salutation. Oṃ rāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Universal Self, Pradyumna; salutation.

Oṃ *yāṃ*, obeisance to the Supreme Being, the Self of the Person, Saṃkarṣaṇa; obeisance. Oṃ *ṣauṃ*, obeisance to the Supreme Being, the Self of the Creator, Vāsudeva; obeisance. One should contemplate the sin as being black in color, bearing a sword and a shield, and possessing its head as the murder of a Brahmin, its two arms as the theft of gold, its heart as the drinking of liquor, and its two hips as violating the teacher’s bed. Its pair of feet are associated with those [sins], its beard and eyes are red, its body hairs are minor sins (*upapātaka*), and it is endowed with every major and minor limb. One should meditate upon this sin within the belly.

Having meditated in this manner: "Oṃ, salutation to the fire, red-colored and triangular, located at the tips of the feet. With its flames, I burn the body from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head. Oṃ laṃ laṃ laṃ, I arrest the arisen fire. In the ether, Oṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ, I meditate upon the seed-syllable of nectar (*amṛtabīja*). With the stream of nectar arising from that, I drench those ashes. Oṃ, for the earth-seed-syllable, Meru-peak is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Atala is the meter (*chanda*), and the venerable Tortoise (*śrī kūrma*) is the deity; the application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of consolidating the drenched ashes."

Having recited from “Oṃ bhūmirbhūmnā” up to “pitaraṃ ca prayantu stuvaḥ,” one says: “Oṃ laṃ laṃ laṃ, obeisance to the dark-colored one, the essence of the earth; I consolidate the mass of ashes that has been flooded. Then, from “ākāśaśarīraṃ brahma” up to “yogyopāsva,” one says: “Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ, by means of the seed-syllable of Śakti, which is all-colored and the self of all, I create a body complete with hands, feet, and other limbs. Oṃ, obeisance to the Sṛṣṭimudrā.

In the ether, I meditate upon the seed-syllable of nectar: "Oṃ vāṃ, salutation to the supreme, salutation to the self of Nivṛtti. From that, meditating with "Oṃ, salutation to the treasury of nectar," and therein having meditated upon the lotus with "Oṃ, salutation to the white, unmanifest lotus," I remember the individual soul (jīva) produced from the presence of the Supreme Brahman: "Oṃ maṃ, salutation to the supreme, appearing like crystal, salutation to the self of the principle of the individual soul (jīvatattva)."

Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha oṃ maṃ haṃ saḥ! O Jīva, come with longing from the presence of the Supreme Brahman to this white lotus. Oṃ maṃ, salutation to the Jīva-mudrā. [Forming the Jīva-mudrā by placing the index finger upon the joint of the thumb. Having displayed it: Oṃ bhaṃ, salutation to the Supreme One of white complexion; salutation to the Self of Prakṛti. From the Jīva, Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation! I create Prakṛti, whose nature consists of the three qualities (guṇas).

Oṃ Bhaṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, who has the luster of crystal; salutation to the Self of the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*). From Prakṛti, I create the intellect whose nature is speech. Oṃ Phaṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, who is pale-red in color; salutation to the Self of ego (*ahaṃkāra*). From the intellect, I create the ego. Oṃ Paṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, who is white and black in color; salutation to the Self of the principle of mind (*manastattva*). From the ego, I create the principle of mind. Oṃ Naṃ. Salutation to the Supreme, who is white in color; salutation to the Self of the subtle element of sound (*śabdatanmātra*).

From the mind, I create the subtle element of sound (*śabda-tanmātra*). From the subtle element of sound—*oṃ hrauṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ sakalarauṃ*—to Sadāśiva, the Lord of Ākāśa, to Īśāna, to Vāsudeva, to the self of the *kalās* beginning with Śānti: *huṃ phaṭ*. [I create] that which has the color of crushed collyrium, is endowed with the organs of speech and hearing, and possesses the quality of sound; *oṃ kaṃ namaḥ*, I create the supreme *ākāśa-tattva*. *Oṃ dhaṃ namaḥ* to the supreme one of blood-red color, the self of the subtle element of touch (*sparśa-tanmātra*): *namaḥ*. I create the subtle element of touch.

From the subtle element of touch (*sparśatanmātra*): *oṃ hraiṃ ṇaṃ sakalaraiṃ*, to the Lord of Wind, to Īśvara, to Tatpuruṣa, to Saṃkarṣaṇa, to the self of the peaceful power (*śāntikalātman*), *huṃ phaṭ*. [I create] the smoky-colored circle, endowed with the skin and the organ of hearing, possessing the qualities of sound and touch: *oṃ khaṃ namaḥ parāya vāyutatvaṃ sṛjāmi*.

From Vāyu: *Oṃ daṃ*, salutation to the Supreme, whose color is light; salutation to the self of the subtle element of form (*rūpa-tanmātra*). I create the subtle element of form. From the subtle element of form: *Oṃ hrūṃ ṇyaṃ hrīṃ sakalarūṃ*, salutation to Rudra, the terrible, the radiant, the Lord of Fire, whose self is the *vidyā-kalā*. *Huṃ phaṭ*! [I create] the triangular [fire], of pale-red color, endowed with the qualities of sound, touch, and form, and possessed of the faculty of sight. *Oṃ gaṃ*, salutation to the Supreme; I create the fire-principle (*agni-tattva*).

Oṃ Thaṃ, salutation to the Supreme Agni; salutation to the one of white complexion, whose essence is the subtle element of taste (rasa-tanmātra). I create the subtle element of taste. From the subtle element of taste: Oṃ Hrīṃ Ṣaṃ Hrīṃ Sakalarīṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the Lord of the Waters, to Vāmadeva, the bearer of the bow, whose essence is the *pratiṣṭhā* kalā—Huṃ Phaṭ! [I create] the water-element (ap-tattva), accompanied by the organs of taste and excretion, endowed with the qualities of sound, touch, form, and taste, white in color, and shaped like a half-moon. Oṃ Ghaṃ, salutation to the Supreme; I create the water-element.

Because of its authority: *Oṃ taṃ namaḥ parāya sitavarṇāya gandhatanmātrātmane namaḥ*. I create the subtle element of smell (*gandhatanmātra*). From the subtle element of smell: *Oṃ hrāṃ jhaṃ laṃ hrīṃ sakalarāṃ pṛthivyadhipataye viṣṇave sadyojātāya nārāyaṇāya nivṛttikalātmane huṃ phaṭ*. [I create] that which has a yellow luster, is square, is endowed with the sense organs of smell and procreation, possesses the qualities of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—*Oṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ parāya pṛthivītatvaṃ sṛjāmi*. (I create the earth-principle.)

Thus, I fashion this divine body, composed of the five elements, consisting of the seven constituents (dhātus), and measuring ninety-six finger-breadths in length. Oṃ ṣauṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Parameṣṭhin, Vāsudeva; salutation. Oṃ yāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Puruṣa, Saṃkarṣaṇa; salutation. Oṃ rāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Viśva, Pradyumna; salutation. Oṃ vāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Nivṛtti, Aniruddha; salutation. Oṃ lāṃ, salutation to the Supreme, the Self of Sarva, the illustrious Nārāyaṇa; salutation.

Oṃ maṃ, salutation to the supreme one who has the luster of crystal; salutation to the self of the principle of life (jīvatattva). Oṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaralavaśaṣasa ha oṃ maṃ haṃ saha he jīva! Come from the white lotus with longing to my heart-lotus. Above: Oṃ, salutation to the awakened lotus. With golden jars filled with the nectar produced therefrom, held in the hands of divine women, I consecrate myself. I worship my own body, which is pure, sinless, and fit for the propitiation of Hari.

Oṃ, salutations to our gurus. Regarding the mantra for the Mātṛkā-nyāsa: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi); the Devī Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ); Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā); the consonants are the seeds (bījāni); the vowels are the powers (śaktayaḥ). The application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of the complete realization of the mantra. Oṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, salutations with the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ). Oṃ iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā with the two index fingers (tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā). Oṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vaṣaṭ with the two middle fingers (madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ).

Oṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ, to the two ring fingers, huṃ. Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, to the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ. Oṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ, to the nails and palms, phaṭ. Thus is the six-limbed assignment (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa). [One should meditate upon the Goddess] whose face, arms, feet, heart, belly, and chest are fashioned from the distinctions of the fifty letters; whose body is radiant, her hair matted, who wears a digit of the moon, and who is as white as the moon and jasmine.

I bow to that Bhāratī, who bears the marks of a rosary, a stream of blood, and a water-pot in her excellent hands; who has three eyes, is seated upon a lotus, possesses a will-power that is as if magical, and carries the weight of full breasts and hips. Now follows the *Mātṛkā-nyāsa* beginning with Keśava and others: Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to Keśava and Kīrti on the forehead. Oṃ Āṃ, salutation to Nārāyaṇa and Kānti on the face. Oṃ Iṃ, salutation to Mādhava and Tuṣṭi. Oṃ Iṃ, salutation to Govinda and Puṣṭi on the two eyes. Oṃ Uṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu and Dhṛti.

Oṃ Ūṃ, salutation to Madhusūdana and Śānti at the two ears. Oṃ Ṛṃ, salutation to Trivikrama and Kriyā. Oṃ Ṝṃ, salutation to Vāmana and Dayā at the two nostrils. Oṃ LṚṃ, salutation to Śrīdhara and Medhā. Oṃ Lṝṃ, salutation to Hṛṣīkeśa and Harṣa at the two cheeks. Oṃ Eṃ, salutation to Padmanābha and Śraddhā. Oṃ Aiṃ, salutation to Dāmodara and Lajjā at the two rows of teeth. Oṃ Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudeva and Lakṣmī.

Oṃ auṃ, salutation to Saṃkarṣaṇa and Sarasvatī on the two lips. Oṃ aṃ, salutation to Pradyumna and Prīti on the tip of the tongue. Oṃ aḥ, salutation to Aniruddha and Rati on the circle of the face. Oṃ kaṃ, salutation to Śaṅkhin and Chāyā; oṃ khaṃ, salutation to Cakrin and Jāyā; oṃ gaṃ, salutation to Gadī and Durgā; oṃ ghaṃ, salutation to Khaḍgin and Satyā; oṃ ṅaṃ, salutation to Śārṅgin and Prabhā—on the right arm, divided into five parts.

Oṃ caṃ, salutation to Halin and Vāṇī; Oṃ chaṃ, salutation to Musalin and Vilāsinī; Oṃ jaṃ, salutation to Śūlin and Layā; Oṃ jhaṃ, salutation to Pāśin and Vinatā; Oṃ ñaṃ, salutation to Aṅkuśin and Viśvā—thus in five divisions on the left arm. Oṃ ṭaṃ, salutation to Mukunda and Vimada; Oṃ ṭhaṃ, salutation to Nanda and Sunandā; Oṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to Nandin and Smṛti; Oṃ ḍhaṃ, salutation to Nara and Jarjhī.

Oṃ ṇaṃ, salutation to Narakajit and Samṛddhi—thus on the right foot. Oṃ taṃ, salutation to Hari and Śuddhi. Oṃ thaṃ, salutation to Kṛṣṇa and Buddhi. Oṃ daṃ, salutation to Satya and Bhukti. Oṃ dhaṃ, salutation to Sattva and Mati. Oṃ naṃ, salutation to Śauri and Kṣamā—thus on the left foot. Oṃ paṃ, salutation to Śūra and Ramā. Oṃ phaṃ, salutation to Janārdana and Umā—on the sides of the belly. Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Bhūdhara and Kledinī—on the back.

Oṃ Bhaṃ, obeisance to Vaikuṇṭha and Vasudhā at the anus. Oṃ Maṃ, obeisance to Viśvamūrti and Saṃklinna at the urethra. Oṃ Yaṃ, obeisance to Puruṣottama and Prathā at the navel. Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to Bala and Aparā at the abdomen. Oṃ Laṃ, obeisance to Balānuja and Dhāraṇā at the heart. Oṃ Vaṃ, obeisance to Bāla and Sūkṣma at the throat. Oṃ Śaṃ, obeisance to Viṣaghna and Sandhi at [the arms]. Oṃ Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Vṛṣa and Prajñā at the breasts.

Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to Haṃsaprabhā; Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Varāhaniśā—at the two arms. Oṃ kṣaṃ oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ kṣrauṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya kṣaṃ, obeisance to Nṛsiṃha and Mohā—at the mouth. Of this glorious eight-syllabled great mantra (mahāmantra): the internal witness Nārāyaṇa is the seer (ṛṣi); the divine Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ); the Supreme Self Nārāyaṇa is the deity (devatā); *am* is the seed-syllable (bīja); *hrīṃ* is the power (śakti); *mam* is the pin (kīlaka); the field is the supreme ether (paramavyoma); the principle (tattva) is the intellect (buddhi); the color is white and so forth; the accent is udātta and so forth; the application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of propitiating the Blessed Lord.

The *karanyāsa* (finger-placement): *oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ yaṃ oṃ oṃ naṃ oṃ oṃ ṇāṃ oṃ oṃ moṃ oṃ oṃ yaṃ oṃ oṃ nāṃ oṃ oṃ rāṃ oṃ*. Beginning from the right index finger and beginning from the left index finger, [place them] on the joints ending with the little fingers. On the joints ending with the little fingers: *oṃ rāṃ oṃ* on the navel with the thumb and little finger; *oṃ yaṃ oṃ* on the genitals with all fingers except the thumbs; *oṃ ṇāṃ oṃ* likewise on the knees; *oṃ yaṃ oṃ* on the two feet with all fingers.

Oṃ oṃ oṃ with the middle fingers at the center of the head; oṃ naṃ oṃ with the index and middle fingers on the two eyes; oṃ moṃ oṃ with the thumb and ring fingers on the face; oṃ nāṃ oṃ with the thumb and index fingers on the heart. Oṃ kruddholkāya svāhā, homage to the heart of knowledge; oṃ maholkāya svāhā, svāhā to the head for sovereignty; oṃ vīrolkāya svāhā, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock for power; oṃ vidyulkāya svāhā, huṃ to the armor for strength.

*Oṃ sahasrolkāya svāhā vīryāyāstrāya phaṭ | Oṃ tejolkāya svāhā tejase netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ |* The visualization (*dhyāna*): Four-armed, with a magnificent body, attended by weapons such as the discus; resembling a dark cloud, with eyes as broad as lotus petals; wearing yellow garments, gentle, with a face like the bright moon; possessing a beautiful smile and lips of fine copper-red; adorned with earrings blazing with jewels; having beautiful eyebrows, a forehead, and a crown, with hair thickly curled.

Having thus meditated upon the Lord of the gods, who has a gentle tilaka on his forehead made of white clay like a lamp, who is adorned with shimmering bracelets, armlets, necklaces, and the Kaustubha gem; who possesses a radiant, brilliant complexion and is graced by the forest of Malaya; who shines with the luster of a thousand suns and is further embellished by ornaments; whose limbs are anointed with divine sandalwood and decorated with celestial garlands; and who sits comfortably upon a beautiful golden throne together with Śrī and Bhūmi—one should become intent upon the recitation of the mantra.
Meditating thus—[on the eight forms] white, golden, black, red like saffron, resembling the filaments of a lotus, and [the rest] possessing all colors—one should recite the mantra.

The Procedure for the Twelve-Syllable Mantra: For this glorious twelve-syllable great mantra (*mahāmantra*), Śrī Vāsudeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*); the goddess Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); the Supreme Self, Vāsudeva, is the deity (*devatā*); *Aṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *Krom* is the power (*śakti*); white is the color; intellect (*buddhi*) is the principle (*tattva*); the supreme ether (*paramavyoman*) is the field (*kṣetra*); and its application (*viniyoga*) is in recitation (*japa*) for the purpose of propitiating the Blessed Lord. The ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*): Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ Yaṃ Oṃ Oṃ Namaḥ Oṃ Oṃ Vāṃ Oṃ Oṃ Moṃ Oṃ Oṃ Deṃ Oṃ Oṃ Bhaṃ Oṃ Oṃ Suṃ Oṃ Oṃ Gaṃ Oṃ Oṃ Vāṃ Oṃ Oṃ Vaṃ Oṃ Oṃ.

The ritual placement on the body (*dehanyāsa*) begins from the right palm up to the little finger, and from the left palm up to the little finger: *Oṃ suṃ oṃ*: with the thumb and little finger at the navel. *Oṃ deṃ oṃ*: with the thumb and index finger at the secret place. *Oṃ vāṃ oṃ*: with all fingers except the thumb at both knees. *Oṃ yaṃ oṃ*: with all fingers at both feet. *Oṃ oṃ oṃ*: with the thumb at the front part of the head. *Oṃ naṃ oṃ*: with the index finger at the right side of the head. *Oṃ moṃ oṃ*: with the ring finger at the back.

Oṃ bhaṃ oṃ with the little finger on the north; oṃ gaṃ oṃ with the middle finger in the center of the head; oṃ vaṃ oṃ with the index and middle fingers on the two eyes; oṃ teṃ oṃ with the thumb and ring finger on the mouth; oṃ vāṃ oṃ with the thumb and index finger on the heart; oṃ oṃ oṃ for knowledge, *namaḥ* to the heart; oṃ naṃ oṃ for sovereignty, *svāhā* to the head; oṃ moṃ oṃ for power, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock; oṃ bhaṃ oṃ for strength, *huṃ* to the armor.

*Oṃ gaṃ oṃ tejase netrābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ vaṃ oṃ vīryāya astrāya phaṭ*. *Oṃ teṃ oṃ udarāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ vāṃ oṃ pṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ suṃ oṃ bāhubhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ deṃ oṃ ūrubhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ vāṃ oṃ jānubhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ yaṃ oṃ pādābhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ kirīṭa-mudrāyai namaḥ* on the head. *Oṃ śrīvatsa-mudrāyai namaḥ* on the right breast. *Oṃ kaustubha-mudrāyai namaḥ* on the left breast.

Oṃ, salutation to the Vanamālā-mudrā at the throat; Oṃ, salutation to the Cakra-mudrā; Oṃ, salutation to the Padma-mudrā on the right side; Oṃ, salutation to the Śaṅkha-mudrā; Oṃ, salutation to the Gadā-mudrā on the left side; Oṃ, salutation to the Garuḍa-mudrā at the tips of the feet. The visualization: [He is] four-armed, with noble limbs, endowed with all the auspicious marks (lakṣaṇas), possessing the luster of pure crystal, and radiant like ten thousand moons. He has a beautiful smile, lovely reddish lips, and eyes extending as far as his ears.

He was free from the glow of the ruby, yet beautifully adorned by the luster of his teeth; broad-chested, long-armed, with a face like the serene moon; possessing beautiful eyebrows, a fine forehead, and a lovely countenance, with hair that was thick and curled; radiant as a thousand flashes of lightning, clad in pure yellow garments; his hands and feet were like lotuses, and his eyes were as long as white water-lilies; marked with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, adorned with a crown and all other ornaments, bearing the lotus, discus, mace, and conch, with the Kaustubha gem upon his breast.

His limbs were anointed with divine perfumes and adorned with celestial garlands; he sat at ease upon the vast coils of the serpent Śeṣa, O Four-faced One. The Lord was accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi, his forehead marked with white clay in the form of an upright *puṇḍra* tilaka, which shone like millions of fierce suns. He was resplendent and difficult to behold, with spreading masses of radiance that seemed to converge from all sides—like ten million moons, ten million suns, and ten million lightning-flashes or fires of universal destruction—emanating from the entire circle of his body.

One whose impurities have been destroyed should meditate upon [the deity] illuminating the entire world—[visualizing him] as white, black, smoke-colored, dark-blue, resembling a star, like crystal, like a conch, red, white, crimson, having the form of darkness, or yellow in color; thus one should meditate on the mantra consisting of twelve syllables. Having meditated in this way, [one should contemplate] the forms of the six limbs: for the six [deities], the white water-lily (kumuda), the bandhūka flower, the blue lotus (asitotpala), the lotus filament (abjakesara), the lotus (ambhoja), and the excellence of the atasī flower. Thus it is said.

Having meditated thus: "I meditate upon myself as the Supreme Lord manifest, bearing divine weapons, garments, garlands, ointments, the Kaustubha gem, a forest garland, the Śrīvatsa mark, and divine characteristics," and having worshipped the deposited seed-syllables with perfumes and other offerings, one should thereafter worship the Blessed One seated in the center of the heart-lotus with mental services (mānasopacāra) ending with the fire-oblation (homa), according to the procedure to be described.

The procedure for the mental sacrifice (*mānasayāga*) is now described: here, the *layayāga* is performed by worshipping the retinue residing within the body of the root mantra, either in the support of the heart-lotus, or wherever else, or in the form of the Lord. The worship of the King of Mantras in the center of the pericarp and of Lakṣmī and the others on the filaments is called *bhoga*. The worship of the lotuses and so forth individually is called *adhikāra*.

Having thus understood the stages of dissolution (*laya*), enjoyment (*bhoga*), and authority (*adhikāra*), one should invoke [the deity] situated in the sky at the end of the *nāda* within the center of the heart-lotus by means of the sacrificial rite called *bhoga*. One should worship according to the path to be described hereafter: having assumed the lotus posture (*padmāsana*) or another such seat, having formed the *brahmāñjali* at the navel, with the body straight and the eyes fixed on the tip of the nose, and without the teeth touching the teeth.

Placing the tongue against the palate, with the head slightly bent and the two arms relaxed, the preceptor should withdraw the external senses into the mind; the mind into the intellect (*buddhi*); and having established the intellect within the sphere of pure knowledge (*jñāna*), he should perform the ultimate rite through the cultivation of that knowledge. He should then contemplate the *ādhāra* and the other centers, divided into four stages between the navel and the perineum, reciting in sequence: "Oṃ, salutation to our thighs."

Between the navel and the genitals: *oṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ*, obeisance to the Support (*ādhāra*), which consists of the five elements—earth, water, fire, air, and space; which abides within the manifestation of one’s own being; and which is peaceful, devoid of activity, white, smiling with its face turned inward, and embraced [by the upper element]. I meditate upon the Support. Above: *jñauṃ ṣrūṃ*, obeisance to Kūrma, who has the form of the Fire of Time (*kālāgni*), who is endowed with the qualities of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, and who abides within the manifestation of the mass of flames.

I meditate upon the Tortoise, endowed with the tortoise-mudrā, having the face of a tortoise, resembling molten gold, bearing the conch and discus, and seated upon a svastika. Above him: Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to Ananta, who abides within the wealth and enjoyments of his own [realm], and who is joined with the [five organs]: Ñaṃ Jhaṃ Jaṃ Chaṃ Caṃ—speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals.

I meditate upon Ananta, who resembles an infinite number of suns, adorned with a thousand hoods, possessing a thousand arms, supporting the earth with his joined palms, and holding a white lotus, a conch, a rosary, and displaying the gesture of fearlessness. Above: *Oṃ bhūṃ*, salutation to the Earth (*Bhūmi*), who resides within the golden splendor, who is endowed with the ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose, and who is the essence of the syllables *ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ*.

I meditate upon the Earth, whose limbs are composed entirely of jewels and gold, radiant like the splendor of the rainy season, seated upon a lotus throne, and holding a lotus and joined palms. At the navel: *Oṃ vaṃ*, salutation to the Ocean of Milk, the essence of nectar, who abides within the manifestation, who is endowed with the principle of the mind (*manastattva*), and who possesses the syllable *paṃ*. I meditate upon the Ocean of Milk: white as a full-blown *kunda* flower, bearing smooth white matted locks, blowing a conch shell adorned with strings of pearls, with all its limbs expansive, its two thighs spread apart, and its knees and feet extended.

Above, [I offer] obeisance to the infinite-petaled lotus, endowed with the principle of ego (*ahaṃkāra-tattva*), which abides within the splendor of the sprout-like petals of its own seed-vessel. I meditate upon the Lotus: radiant with palms and soles of feet dark as a ripe mango fruit, with red eyes, disheveled hair, and a smiling face; seated in the lotus posture (*padmāsana*), encircled by a swarm of bees, with very long legs, and marked with the lotus gesture (*padmamudrā*). Within that, in the southeast, [I offer] obeisance to Dharma, endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhi-tattva*), who abides within the splendor of discernment.

I meditate upon the embodiment of Dharma, who has the color of snow, the face of a lion, and is the head of Dharma. In the southwest (Nairṛti): Oṃ Vaṃ, salutation to the one endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*), who abides within the power of discernment (*viveka*), the embodiment of knowledge (*jñāna*). I meditate upon the embodiment of Knowledge, who has the luster of a clear crystal and the face of a lion. In the northwest (Vāyavya): Oṃ Baṃ, salutation to Vairāgya (Dispassion), who is endowed with the principle of intellect and abides within the power of discernment. I meditate upon the embodiment of Dispassion, who has the brilliance of a pearl and the face of a lion.

In the northeast: Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Aiśvarya (Sovereignty), who is endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*), who abides at the end of the manifestation of ignorance (*avidyāvibhava*). I meditate upon the one who is moon-colored, lion-faced, and whose head is Sovereignty. In the east: Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Adharma (Unrighteousness), who is endowed with the principle of intellect, who abides at the end of the manifestation of ignorance. I meditate upon the one who is the color of a ruby (*padmarāga*), lion-faced, and whose head is Unrighteousness.

In the south: Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Ignorance (Ajñāna), who is endowed with the principle of intellect (buddhitattva), who abides at the end of the manifestation of ignorance (avidyā-vibhava). I meditate upon him, who is the color of coral and has the face of a lion, as the head of Ignorance. In the west: Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Non-detachment (Avairāgya), who is endowed with the principle of intellect, who abides at the end of the manifestation of ignorance. I meditate upon him, who is fire-colored and has the face of a lion, as the head of Ignorance. In the north: Oṃ baṃ, salutation to Sovereignty-deficiency (Anaiśvarya), who is endowed with the principle of intellect, who abides at the end of the manifestation of ignorance.

I meditate upon the one with the color of a pomegranate fruit and the face of a lion, who stands at the root of ignorance. Between the directions of the East and the Northeast: *Oṃ baṃ*, salutation to the Ṛgveda, who is endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*), who abides within the expanse of the manifestation of speech. I meditate upon the Ṛgveda, golden-hued and horse-faced. Between the directions of the East and the Southeast: *Oṃ yaṃ*, salutation to the Yajurveda, who is endowed with the principle of intellect and who abides within the expanse of the manifestation of speech. I meditate upon the Yajurveda, the color of a campaka flower and horse-faced.

Between Nirṛti and Varuṇa: Oṃ Baṃ, salutations to the Sāmaveda, who is endowed with the principle of intellect (buddhitattva), who abides within the manifestation of the expansion of speech. I meditate upon the Sāmaveda, who has the color of a firefly and the face of a horse. Between Vāyu and Varuṇa: Oṃ Baṃ, salutations to the Atharvaṇaveda, who is endowed with the principle of intellect and who abides within the manifestation of the expansion of speech.

I meditate upon the Atharvaṇa Veda, which has the color of yellow orpiment and the face of a horse. In the intermediate direction between Īśāna and Soma (the northeast), [I offer: *Oṃ Baṃ*, salutation to the Kṛta Yuga, which is endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*), which abides from the moment of a *truṭi* until the end of the cosmic manifestation, and which is the Kṛta Yuga itself. I meditate upon the Kṛta Yuga, which has the face of a bull-king and the color of a ripe mango fruit. Within the fire of destruction, [I offer: *Oṃ Baṃ*, salutation to the Tretā Yuga, which is endowed with the principle of intellect, which abides from the moment of a *truṭi* until the end of the cosmic manifestation, and which is the Tretā Yuga itself.

I meditate upon the Dvāpara Yuga, whose face is like that of the lordly bull, resembling the flax flower (*atasīpuṣpa*). Between the southern Rākṣasa and [the deity], *Oṃ Baṃ*, salutation to the Dvāpara Yuga, who is endowed with the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*), who abides from the moment of a truti until the end of the cosmic manifestation (*kalpa*). I meditate upon the Dvāpara Yuga, whose face is like that of the lordly bull and whose color is like a blue lotus. Between Soma and Sāmīraṇa, *Oṃ Baṃ*, salutation to the Kali Yuga, who is endowed with the principle of intellect, who abides from the moment of a truti until the end of the cosmic manifestation.

I meditate upon the Kali Yuga, white in color and with the face of a lordly bull. I meditate upon these [ages] as sixteen-year-old youths, possessing all the marks of a perfect man, endowed with fine garments, beautiful flowers, and excellent ornaments; holding a conch, a lotus, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness; with their heads resting upon the wheel of the Adheya; and with their inner faculties surrendered to the Supreme through the performance of mantra for the sake of the perfection of one's own self. Above [this], *Oṃ raṃ vaṃ haṃ, obeisance to Kālacakra, the refuge of the three abodes, who dwells within the revolving power of Māyā, Hrīṃ*.

I meditate upon the King of Weapons (Hetirāja), who resembles the fire of the sun at the end of an eon, standing in the midst of his own circle of rays, with hands occupied by his own mudrās, and leaping forth. Above, [I offer] *oṃ bhaṃ* to the Unmanifest Lotus (*avyaktapadma*), which is endowed with the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛti-tattva*), situated within the glory of its secondary functions and movements; salutations! I meditate upon the Unmanifest Lotus, which is radiant like snow, gold, and fire; whose stalk arises from the northwest; which is peaceful, eight-armed, and situated upon a *svastika*; which is gentle, upward-facing, well-established as the substratum of all transformations, and has the form of a lotus in the heart.

Above: *Oṃ maṃ*, salutation to the individual self (*jīvātman*), who is of the nature of the conscious sun (*cidāditya*), who abides within the manifestation of the multitude of pure digits (*vimalā-kalā-jāla*), who is the mass of consciousness (*cidghana*), eternal, unmanifest, the treasury of all powers, formless, and whose form is the light of consciousness. I meditate upon the individual soul (*jīva*) which possesses the luster of a crystal stone. In the center of the body: *Oṃ*, salutation to the Suṣumnā channel (*suṣumnā-nāḍikā*).

I meditate upon the central channel named Suṣumnā, which, originating from the bulb of the navel, has ascended through the aperture of Brahmā along the path of the sun; it has pierced the subterranean realm (Pātāla) and reached its own domain through the anus; like a string of jewels upon a thread, it is established within itself as the object of all volitions, radiant with the three lights. Above the individual soul (jīvātman), [I offer salutations] to the Power of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahma-śakti), whose form consists of various multitudes of mantras: Oṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance!

I meditate upon the Supreme Vāk-bhramarī, the mother of all mantras, who resounds with the sound born of the phonemes from 'A' to 'Ha' in the form of a continuous stream; she who is renowned in the heaven of Śabdabrahman as the power of those whose nature is peace. Above her, in the sky at the end of the Nāda, is "Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya."

I meditate upon the God who is peaceful, eternal, the very nature of consciousness, perpetually satisfied, stainless, possessing all forms yet formless; who, out of a desire to bestow grace upon His devotees, has assumed a form despite being formless; who is incomparable, and whose splendor is equal to a thousand suns, fires, moons, hundreds of thousands, and tens of millions. Having thus meditated, one should then contemplate with the mantra: *Oṃ asmadga urubhyaḥ namaḥ*. Then, upon the petals of the heart-lotus starting from the east, one should worship: *Oṃ utkarṣiṇyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ jñānāyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ kriyāyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ yoginyai namaḥ*.

Oṃ, obeisance to Prahvā. Oṃ, obeisance to Satyā. Oṃ, obeisance to Īśānī. In the pericarp: Oṃ, obeisance to Anugrahā. Oṃ, the Puruṣa with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet, having pervaded the earth on all sides, transcended it by the measure of ten fingers. Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva; come, come to the center of the pericarp of the unmanifest lotus! The Puruṣa alone is all this—whatever has been and whatever is to be. He is the Lord of immortality, as well as that which grows through food.

I offer a seat. Welcome, O Lord of the gods; accept my presence, O Acyuta. Accept this mental worship, contemplated according to its true nature. Om, salutation to the Āvāhana-mudrā. Om, salutation to the Sthāpana-mudrā. Om, salutation to the Sannidhāna-mudrā. Om, salutation to the Sannirodha-mudrā. Om, salutation to the Sāṃmukhya-mudrā. Om, salutation to the Prārthanā-mudrā. Above the head: Om, salutation to Gaṅgā, who resides in the space within the lotus.

"I meditate upon the Gaṅgā, consisting of nectar, which has descended from the head of the Blessed One by way of the *suṣumṇā* path. Having thus meditated, one should mentally offer the *arghya* and other oblations with that nectar-like water. "Such is His greatness; yet the Puruṣa is greater than this. All beings constitute but one quarter of Him; His three quarters are the immortal in heaven. I offer the water for washing the feet (*pādya*). "The Puruṣa rose up three quarters high, while one quarter of Him remained here again. Thence He strode out in all directions, pervading both the eating and the non-eating worlds. I offer the *arghya*.

From that, Virāj was born; from Virāj, Puruṣa was born. Once born, he extended beyond [the earth], behind, below, and before. I offer water for sipping (ācamana). Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Vāsudeva; I prepare the seat of the mantra. Upon the right filaments of the lotus of the Deity: Oṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Śrī. Come, come! I meditate upon Śrī, whose nature is the Sound-Brahman (Śabdabrahman) and who consists of all powers. Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī; I offer the lotus-seat (padmāsana).

I offer water for the feet consisting of nectar. I offer the respectful oblation (*arghya*). I offer water for sipping (*ācamanīya*). I prepare the seat of mantras. For the mantra of the Goddess Śrī: Maṅkaṇa is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); the Goddess Śrī is the deity (*devatā*); *Śrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *Hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*); *Klīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*); the application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of complete worship. *Oṃ śrāṃ*, salutation to the heart. *Oṃ śrīṃ*, *svāhā* to the head. *Oṃ śrūṃ*, *vaṣaṭ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*). *Oṃ śraiṃ*, *hum* to the armor (*kavaca*). *Oṃ śrauṃ*, *vauṣaṭ* to the two eyes.

Oṃ śraḥ astrāya phaṭ | Oṃ, salutation to the lotus gesture (kamalamudrā). To the left of the deity: Oṃ bhūṃ, salutation to the Earth; come, come! I meditate upon the Earth composed of all powers. Oṃ, salutation to the Earth; I prepare [the seat]. I offer water for the feet consisting of nectar. I offer the arghya. I offer water for sipping (ācamanīya). I prepare the seat of mantra. Regarding the mantra of Bhūdevī: Kaṇva is the seer (ṛṣi); Gāyatrī is the meter (chanda); Bhū is the deity (devatā); Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja); Śrīṃ is the power (śakti).

*Klīṃ* is the *kīlaka*. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of propitiation. *Oṃ hrāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Oṃ hrūṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*. *Oṃ hraiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*. *Oṃ hrauṃ* to the two eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ hraḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. *Oṃ* to the lotus-gesture (*kamala-mudrā*), *namaḥ*. I shall perform the visualization of the retinue (*parivārakalpana*). Upon the petals of the lotus of the yoga-posture, in the twelve petals starting from the east:

Om, salutation to Śrīvatsa; Om, salutation to Vanamālā; Om, salutation to Yogamāyā; Om, salutation to Vaiṣṇavī; Om, salutation to Vimalā; Om, salutation to Sṛṣṭi; Om, salutation to Utkarṣiṇī; Om, salutation to Prajñā; Om, salutation to Satyā; Om, salutation to Aiśānī; Om, salutation to Anukampā; Om, salutation to Pitāmahī. Having meditated upon these as holding a handful of flowers.

Om, salutation to Vyāpti; Om, salutation to Kānti; Om, salutation to Tṛpti; Om, salutation to Śraddhā; Om, salutation to Vidyā; Om, salutation to Jayā; Om, salutation to Kṣamā; Om, salutation to Śānti. Surrounding that, in the second enclosure: Om, salutation to Śaṅkhin; Om, salutation to Cakrin; Om, salutation to Gadin; Om, salutation to Śārṅgin; Om, salutation to Pāśin; Om, salutation to Aṅkuśin.

Oṃ, obeisance to Indra; Oṃ, obeisance to Agni; Oṃ, obeisance to Yama; Oṃ, obeisance to Nairṛti; Oṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa; Oṃ, obeisance to Vāyu; Oṃ, obeisance to Soma; Oṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Outside the third enclosure, facing the Blessed One: Oṃ kṣam, obeisance to Vainateya. In the northeastern direction: Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣvaksena. I meditate upon these [deities] facing the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence.

Oṃ, salutations to the Blessed One Vāsudeva, accompanied by Śrī and Bhū; I prepare a seat for the bath. "With the Puruṣa as the oblation... summer is this, autumn the oblation. I offer the bath. Oṃ, I prepare a seat for ornaments. "Seven were his enclosing sticks... the Puruṣa as the sacrificial animal. Oṃ, I offer the garment. "That sacrifice... and the Ṛṣis who [were present]. I offer the sacred thread (upavīta). "From that sacrifice, from which all was offered... and those that are domestic."

Oṃ, I offer fragrance. From that sacrifice in which everything was offered... from it the Yajus was born. Oṃ, I offer flowers. From that the horses were born... and goats and sheep. Oṃ, I offer incense. When they divided the Puruṣa... Oṃ, I offer light. Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, accompanied by Śrī and Bhū; I prepare a seat for the food offering. The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth... from his two feet the Śūdra was born.

Oṃ, I offer this food-offering consisting of nectar. From the mind the moon was born... from the vital breath (prāṇa) the wind was born. Oṃ, I offer betel-leaf. Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, accompanied by Śrī and Bhū. With these offerings—beginning with the invocation and ending with the betel-leaf—which have been rendered pure through the formal resolve (saṃkalpa), which are imperishable, auspicious, and consist of contact-based, ritual, and edible forms arising from the seven worlds, as prescribed, possessing the most excellent characteristics, composed of nectar, and accompanied by Śrī and Bhūmi...

Be content. Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One Vāsudeva, accompanied by Śrī and Bhū; I offer cows and vehicles adorned with all ornaments. From the navel arose... thus they fashioned the worlds. Oṃ, I take refuge at the feet of Vāsudeva, who is accompanied by Śrī and Bhū. With eyes overflowing with tears of bliss, I surrender myself, along with my sons, grandsons, and wife, unto the Blessed One.

"Oṃ kṣaṃ, obeisance to the Cow-Seal (dhenumudrā) who grants all desired objects. Having displayed the Surabhi-seal, [one says: "Be satisfied by the substances produced therefrom, which consist of nectar. One meditates upon the *añjali* gesture filled with golden flowers. Thus, having formed the *añjali*, one should utter the root mantra for each of the exhalation (*recaka*), inhalation (*pūraka*), and retention (*kumbhaka*) within that [gesture], and having meditated upon [the deity] resembling fire, sun, and moon, saying "Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, come, come," one should restrain [the breath].

Having placed that deity upon his head, having again offered an *arghya* and a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), having displayed the root-mudrā (*mūlamudrā*), and having displayed the respective mudrās for Lakṣmī and the others, having recited the root mantra (*mūlamanu*) as many times as possible, and having praised him with hymns, he should propitiate Vāsudeva together with Śrī and Bhūmi. Now, the procedure for the mental fire-sacrifice (*mānasāgnikārya*) is described.

In the center of the navel-cakra, [one should place] *oṃ gaṃ bhaṃ hrīṃ* for the triangle surrounded by the three qualities (*triguṇa*); *oṃ raṃ*, salutation to the fire-chamber joined with the primary fire (*pradhānāgni*). I meditate upon the fire situated in the triangular sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) within the navel-cakra. By churning the fire-drill of meditation, I generate the fire of consciousness (*cidagni*). I meditate upon the fire whose essence is Vāsudeva—pure, consecrated, blazing, and with upward-pointing flames. Having thus meditated:

Beginning with “*aditenumanyasva*” and ending with “*devasavitaḥ prasuva*,” one should meditate on the sprinkling with nectar (*amṛta*). Then, having invoked the mantra-form of the Lord into the tip of that flame with the mantra, “*oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya āgacchāgaccha*,” and having restrained [the deity], one should offer the *arghya* and other honors with nectar as before, while recollecting [the ritual]. One should then meditate on the nectar-like clarified butter (*ājya*) falling from above the lotus into a golden vessel by way of the *suṣumṇā* channel.

Then, having satiated with clarified butter (ājya) the form of the mantra situated within the triangle of the navel-cakra in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), standing at the tip of the flame of the fire of consciousness (cidagni), by means of the root-mantra ending in *svāhā*; and having meditated upon the sprinkling (pariṣecana) beginning with "O Aditi, you who stand in the earth" and ending with "O God Savitar, you have impelled."

Having meditated upon the offering as consisting of nectar (*amṛtamaya*), and having again invoked [the deity] as before—seated at the tip of the flame of the fire of consciousness (*cidagni*) within the *nābhicakra* in the center of the heart-lotus—and having meditated upon him stationed there; then, having visualized to the right a water-pot (*karaka*) filled with water, flowers, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*); and having recollected within that [pot]: "Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Vāsudeva"; and having meditated: "Within that [Vāsudeva], Oṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Śrī—I meditate upon the excellence of the sacrificial ground (*bhūsampatti*) described in the ritual as being the form of Lakṣmī. Thus he meditates.

Then, once again in that same manner as before, having recollected the root mantra (mūlamantra), placing his knees upon the ground with his head bowed, and having offered [the offering] to Viṣṇu, he should contemplate Him as being well-pleased and inclined toward granting grace, saying: "Salutations to You, O Lord of all worlds, O Blessed One whose form is the mantra! I worship You; therefore, dwell within this image and likewise within my heart. Having said this, he should then perform the external worship according to the procedure to be described hereafter. Now, the purification of the mantra: *Oṃ yaṃ vāyave namaḥ*, I dry up the seed-syllables of the mantra.

"Oṃ raṃ, salutation to Agni; I burn the seed-syllables of the mantra. Oṃ laṃ, salutation to Pṛthivī; I flood them with a stream of nectar. Oṃ haṃ, I purify the seed-syllables of the mantra. Having performed this purification in this manner, one should recite the purified mantra one hundred and eight or twenty-eight times on a rosary, encased between the seed-syllable at the beginning and the end. This is the twofold purification of the mantra.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Procedure for the Purification of the Mantras," including the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), the internal sacrifice (*antaryāga*) ending with the placement of mantras (*mantranyāsa*), and the mental fire-ritual (*mānasāgnikārya*), within the *Kriyākairavacandrikā* composed by the venerable Varāhaguru.
The Twenty-eighth Chapter.

Then, having washed all the vessels, and having washed the *galantikā* (drip-stand) on the right side and filled it with water, he places it on his left side. Having worshipped it with "Oṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa, the presiding deity of the vessels for worship beginning with the *vardhanī*," he washes the vessels for the *arghya* and other offerings with the Viṣṇu-Gāyatrī. Having placed a three-tiered footstool (*tripādukā*) in front of the deity or himself, he invokes and worships it upon that stool with "Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to Tretāgni, the presiding deity of the *tripādukā*."

Having placed a vessel-supporting bowl (sthālīkā) upon that, one should invoke and worship the Earth with the mantra "Oṃ Laṃ Pṛthvyai Namaḥ" within it. Upon that, having set down the vessels for water for the feet (pādya), the respectful offering (arghya), and water for sipping (ācamanīya) in the center, to the right, and to the left respectively, and having filled them with filtered water, one should touch them with the Praṇava (Oṃ). Then, into the arghya vessel, one should place the tips of kuśa grass, unbroken rice (akṣata), flowers, fruit, sandalwood paste, sesame seeds, white mustard seeds, and barley; and into the pādya vessel, sesame seeds, dūrvā grass, viṣṇuparṇī, śyāmāka grain, lotus seeds, and unbroken rice.

Having placed cardamom, cloves, camphor, jasmine, *takkola*, and sandalwood in the vessel for the water for rinsing (*ācamanīya-pātra*), one should meditate with the right hand on "Oṃ Raṃ, salutation to the twelve-spoked wheel," and in its center on "Oṃ Haṃ, salutation to the Sun. Having meditated that the substances have been burnt by those blazing rays, one should meditate with the left hand on "Salutation to the white lotus with sixteen petals, which is in full bloom," and in its center on "Oṃ Vaṃ, salutation to the Moon, who consists of nectar and possesses sixteen digits."

Having visualized the ritual substances as sprinkled with the nectar arising therefrom, and having reflected that they are now fit for sacrifice; having meditated upon the Lord with the mantra "Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya" while on both hands, and having touched the substances with them; having consecrated them with the Viṣṇu-Gāyatrī; and having displayed the Surabhi-mudrā with the mantra "Oṃ surabhimudrāyai namaḥ"; one should visualize the vessels as being filled with the nectar produced thereby.

Uttering "Oṃ, I prepare the *arghya*; Oṃ, I prepare the *pādya*; Oṃ, I prepare the *ācamana*," and touching those [substances], one should take a little water from the *arghya* vessel into another vessel. Having placed the support (*ādhāra*) upon the pedestal (*sthalikā*), one should invoke and worship [the deities] by saying "Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu" over the *arghya* vessel, "Oṃ, obeisance to Madhusūdana" over the *pādya* vessel, and "Oṃ, obeisance to Trivikrama" over the *ācamanīya* vessel. Then, placing the *arghya* water contained in the other vessel in the left hand:

Having consecrated [the water] seven times with the root mantra, one should sprinkle the ritual substances and oneself with that water while reciting: *oṃ sahasrāra huṃ phaṭ*. Then, one should prepare the yoga-pīṭha for the deity: *oṃ pṛṃ ḍhṛṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti*; *oṃ hrūṃ, obeisance to Kālapāvaka-Kūrma*; *oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ananta, who supports the square earth-maṇḍala upon his thousand hoods*; *oṃ bhūṃ, obeisance to Bhūmi*. Above that, in the corners starting from the southeast (āgneya):

Om, salutation to Dharma; Om, salutation to Jñāna; Om, salutation to Vairāgya; Om, salutation to Aiśvarya. I meditate upon these as having the form of the feet of the Yoga-seat, human in shape, four-armed, lion-faced, and standing. Om, salutation to Adharma; Om, salutation to Ajñāna; Om, salutation to Avairāgya; Om, salutation to Anaiśvarya. In the center: Om, salutation to Sadāśiva. I meditate upon these as being of reddish hue and similar to those [previously described].

In the spaces between the feet of the Yoga-posture, starting from the east and so forth, I meditate upon these in the form of arrows: *oṃ ṛgvedāya namaḥ*, *oṃ yajurvedāya namaḥ*, *oṃ sāmavedāya namaḥ*, *oṃ atharvavedāya namaḥ*, *oṃ kṛtayugāya namaḥ*, *oṃ tretāyugāya namaḥ*, *oṃ dvāparayugāya namaḥ*, *oṃ kaliyugāya namaḥ*.

Oṃ, salutation to the Vaikārika Ahaṃkāra; Oṃ, salutation to the Taijasa Ahaṃkāra; Oṃ, salutation to the Bhautika Ahaṃkāra—I meditate upon these as being joined in the form of fetters. Oṃ, salutation to the Sattva quality; Oṃ, salutation to the Rajas quality; Oṃ, salutation to the Tamas quality—I meditate upon these in the form of qualities. Oṃ Ṅaṃ Ghaṃ Gaṃ Khaṃ Kaṃ, salutation to the essences of earth, water, fire, air, and ether in the form of brushes.

*Oṃ maṃ*, salutation to the *jīvātman* (individual soul) in the form of the seat. Upon that: *oṃ raṃ*, salutation to the fire-maṇḍala (*agnimaṇḍala*). *Oṃ vaṃ*, salutation to the moon-maṇḍala (*somamaṇḍala*). *Oṃ haṃ*, salutation to the sun-maṇḍala (*sūryamaṇḍala*). Above that: *oṃ*, salutation to the unmanifest lotus (*avyaktapadma*), which is white, possesses twelve petals, is endowed with a vast pericarp and filaments, and consists of the three qualities (*guṇatraya*). *Oṃ*, salutation to the auspicious throne (*bhadrāsana*). Having thus invoked the deities residing within the seat and worshipped them with the four offerings beginning with fragrance (*gandha*), [one should worship] with *oṃ* on the right side of the pedestal.

Having worshipped with "Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā; Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu; Oṃ, salutation to Īśvara"; having worshipped in the north with "Oṃ, salutation to Sanatkumāra; Oṃ, salutation to Sanaka; Oṃ, salutation to Sanandana"; having worshipped in the west with "Oṃ, salutation to Durgā; Oṃ, salutation to Vighneśa; Oṃ, salutation to Nārada"; and having meditated upon [the gurus] in front with "Oṃ, salutation to our immediate gurus (guravaḥ); Oṃ, salutation to our supreme gurus (parama-guravaḥ); Oṃ, salutation to all our gurus (sarva-guravaḥ)."

Thereafter, one should perform the invocation (*āvāhana*). However, if only a single drum (*bherī*) is provided, one should not invoke. When Hari has been brought down by the *suras* and *siddhas*, one should meditate upon Him residing within the heart while He is present in the image; for invocation is simply the act of making [the deity] face [the worshipper]. Nor is there the conceptualization of an entourage (*parivāra*) in that case. But in other instances, such as with a statue and the like, one should wash the vessel of invocation with water, fill it with water using the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), and lift it up from the forehead with both hands.

In that [water], having recited four times according to the specific image either "Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, come, come! or "Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, come, come!", and having invoked [the deity] residing in the heart; having sprinkled that water upon the head of the image with the *kūrca* [grass-bundle]; having visualized [the deity] residing in the vessel as being within the image; having displayed the *āvāhana-mudrā*; having risen slightly and prostrated; having said "Welcome"; having displayed that [same] mudrā; and having displayed the *pratimā-mudrā*.

Having prepared the *sannidhi* (proximity), having displayed the *mudrā*, and having prayed for the presence of Hari at the conclusion of the sacrifice, one should display the *prārthanā-mudrā*. Then, one should display the *sāmmukhya-mudrā* with the mantra: *oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya sammukho bhava*. In the case of a single image (*ekabera*), one should invoke [the deity] from the source according to the prescribed path, and then display the *āvāhana*, *sthāpana*, *sannidhāna*, *sannirodhana*, *sāmmukhya*, and *prārthanā-mudrās*.

Having offered the seat with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), and having performed the placement of the mantras (*mantra-nyāsa*) upon the body of the God without the placement of the hands (*hasta-nyāsa*), one should display the mudrās of the crown, the *śrīvatsa*, the *kaustubha* gem, the forest garland (*vanamālā*), the discus, the conch, the mace, the lotus, and Garuḍa. Then, one should say: "O All-pervading One, Lord of all worlds, Viṣṇu, Conqueror, Master, Hari! Today, with devotion, I shall worship You with offerings such as the *arghya* and other enjoyments in due order. At this time, I shall worship the Blessed Janārdana according to the rules and according to my capacity, with divine offerings including the *arghya*."

Having thus addressed the Lord of Gods: "Om, we meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our intellects. I offer this *arghya*. Having thus offered the *arghya* upon the head of the God: "Om, Viṣṇu, the protector, strode three steps, and from there he established the laws of righteousness. I offer water for the feet (*pādya*) at his feet. (This is repeated twice. "Om, may the waters purify the earth; may the purified earth purify me; may Brahmaṇaspati purify me."

"May the purifier of Brahmā purify me. Having thus offered water for sipping (ācamana) into the mouth, one should offer the *madhuparka*, which is traditionally defined as honey, milk, curd, and clarified butter—either as a single component or all together—and not omit the *madhuparka*. Having said this, one should present the *madhuparka* with the formula: "Om, obeisance to the Blessed Vāsudeva. Then, having prostrated before the Deity with the eight-limbed salutation (*aṣṭāṅga-praṇipāta*), according to the verse: "With both hands, the head, the feet, the mind, the intellect, and likewise with the ego, I cast myself down upon the surface of the earth."

"I am your servant, O Lord of the World, along with my children and possessions; please always employ me as a messenger for whatever service may be required. Having thus addressed the Lord of Gods, one should arrange the retinue upon the petals of the yoga-seat lotus, starting from the east, in twelve directions: *Oṃ śrīvatsāya namaḥ*, *Oṃ vanamālāyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ yogamāyāyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ vaiṣṇavyai namaḥ*, *Oṃ vimalāyai namaḥ*.

Om, salutation to Sṛṣṭi; Om, salutation to Utkarṣiṇī; Om, salutation to Prajñā; Om, salutation to Satyā; Om, salutation to Aiśānī; Om, salutation to Anukampā; Om, salutation to Pitāmahī—[these are] around the pedestal in the first enclosure (prathamāvaraṇa), starting from the east: Om, salutation to Vyāpti; Om, salutation to Kānti; Om, salutation to Tṛpti; Om, salutation to Śraddhā; Om, salutation to Vidyā; Om, salutation to Jayā; Om, salutation to Kṣamā; Om, salutation to Śānti. Thus.

And [the goddesses] holding chowries; in the second enclosure: *oṃ śaṅkiṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ cakriṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ gadine namaḥ*, *oṃ khaḍgiṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ padmine namaḥ*, *oṃ musaline namaḥ*, *oṃ śārṅgiṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ vanamāline namaḥ*. In the third enclosure: *oṃ indrāya namaḥ*, *oṃ agnaye namaḥ*, *oṃ yamāya namaḥ*, *oṃ nairṛtaye namaḥ*, *oṃ varuṇāya namaḥ*, *oṃ vāyave namaḥ*, *oṃ somāya namaḥ*, *oṃ īśānāya namaḥ*.

Outside the third enclosure, facing the Blessed One, [one should worship] Vainateya. In the northeast, having worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣvaksena," one should prepare the bathing seat. Having worshipped the sandals with "Oṃ, obeisance to the presiding deity of the sandals; Oṃ, obeisance to Ananta," and having recalled the Lord's mounting of the sandals while reciting "This Viṣṇu" and "The three steps," [one performs] the consecration. Recalling the Lord as having arisen with the mantra "Arise."

Having meditated upon [the deity] seated on the bathing throne with the mantra *bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ*, and then having made the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*) "I shall perform the daily bathing of this God of gods," and having performed the purification of its limbs and the recitation for an auspicious day (*puṇyāhavācana*), and having sprinkled the water-jars and the bathing substances; having washed nine jars—made of gold or other metals, or of clay, and wrapped with thread—and having laid down six lines of thread from east to north over a heap of grain in the center of the half-pavilion;

Having placed the pitchers (kalaśas) among them, from Brahmā to Īśāna, and having filled them with ghee, water for washing the feet (pādya), curd, water for the guest-offering (arghya), milk, water for rinsing the mouth (ācamana), honey, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and fruits; and having provided them with cloths, gems, and tufts of grass (kūrca), and covered them with sprouts of the holy fig tree (aśvattha); then, having invoked and worshipped Paravāsudeva, Viṣṇu, Śrīdhara, Madhusūdana, Hṛṣīkeśa, Trivikrama, Padmanābha, Vāmana, and Dāmodara within them—beginning with the ghee and ending with the fruits—in due order; and having covered them with Darbha grass and displayed the discus mudrā (cakramudrā).

Having worshipped the deity seated for the bath with the *arghya* and other offerings as before, one should offer a tooth-stick with the mantra *oṃ tad viṣṇoḥ*, cleanse the tongue with the *Viṣṇugāyatrī*, and offer an *āmalaka* fruit with *oṃ viṣṇornukam*. Then, having performed the sprinkling with *na te viṣṇo* and *āpo hiṣṭhā*, and the cleaning of the hair with a golden comb using *oṃ ato devā avantu*, one should subsequently bathe the deity with the water from the established jars, beginning with the *pādya* and ending with *ghṛta*.
